title: From Security Requirements to Organisational Controls: A Conceptual Traceability Model for Background Verification
content: Background verification of employees involves the movement of personal records between clients and staff members and other sources external to the organisation. Procedures describe the activities but do not always explain the reason for the security measures or who is responsible for ensuring that they are executed. This article attempts to trace security requirements to accountable controls in the background verification process. By drawing upon research into requirements traceability, conceptual research and information security governance, a Security Requirements to Controls Traceability Model is proposed. The model connects each security requirement to a control objective, a procedure, a responsible role and the evidence required to show that the requirement was met. The model also records the information at risk, the reason for the requirement, the review conditions for the control and any approved exceptions. The model is illustrated with an academic verification process. However, the model does not attempt to  determine whether the controls are effective at mitigating the risks that they were intended to address or whether the organisation is in compliance with the laws that it is subject to. The limitations of the model are the selective use of sources in the construction of the model, the reliance upon the judgement of the authors in constructing the model and the lack of testing of the model in the field.
